propositions: Rebar has no mechanism to track eval spend in dollars or enforce a budget cap, requiring manual operator discipline to stay under $200 on Bedrock.

Pre-flight estimates for eval runs must be flat, historically-measured per-sample constants (not live token-count predictions), since the corpus does not record token counts and agentic loops have unpredictable output token cost.
A run's actual spend cannot be finalized with an unpriced Bedrock model id; pricing lookup failure must raise loudly rather than silently recording zero dollars.

The ledger must track per-run metadata (run_id, tier, candidate, tokens, usd, price_table_version) in a committed JSONL file and offer reserve(), finalize(), reconcile(), and print_summary() operations.
Single-writer assumption is explicit and documented: reserve() is not concurrent-safe; runs execute serially via operator control and concurrent eval runners are out of scope.
